{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mo-f","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d3adeb2f5ad8d789f8dbbbc357ca7d473d3d2a31fa20c263365b331fbace26bf","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","source_liveness_sha256":"fdf72d02e75b9589fee5aaf5b83ec9705ff03586f574464e3553a827f9b698d8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Missouri point system: point values by violation, advisory, suspension and revocation thresholds, reinstatement, point reduction, driving while suspended or revoked, failure to appear, and school bus suspensions","heading":"C — The point system: how points are added, sample point values, the advisory, suspension and revocation thresholds, reinstatement, how points come off, driving while suspended or revoked, failure to appear in court, and the school bus suspension","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — The point system: how points are added, sample point values, the advisory, suspension and revocation thresholds, reinstatement, how points come off, driving while suspended or revoked, failure to appear in court, and the school bus suspension
Knowledge domain: how Missouri adds points to a driving record after a moving violation conviction, what common violations are worth, how many points within a given window trigger an advisory, a suspension or a revocation, what reinstatement takes, how points are reduced over time, and the separate consequences for driving while suspended or revoked, failing to appear in court, and failing to stop for a school bus.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and you can lose it by breaking the traffic laws. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
When you are convicted of a traffic violation that happened while your vehicle was moving, the Department is notified and adds points to your driving record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Collecting too many points can cost you your driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
How many points you get depends on the conviction; a speeding conviction may bring two or three points depending on whether the court was municipal, county or state. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Leaving the scene of a traffic crash can bring 12 points and the revocation of your driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
In the guide's list of state law violations, speeding is worth 3 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Careless and imprudent driving is worth 4 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
Knowingly letting an unlicensed driver operate a vehicle is worth 4 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
Failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading students is worth 5 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
A felony involving a motor vehicle is worth 12 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
Getting a driver license through misrepresentation is worth 12 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
Driving with a suspended or revoked driver license is worth 12 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
Reaching a total of 4 points within 12 months gets you a point accumulation advisory from the Department. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A01
Reaching 8 or more points within 18 months gets your driving privilege suspended. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A01
A suspension for 8 points in 18 months lasts 30 days the first time, 60 days the second time, and 90 days the third or any later time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A01
Your driving privilege is revoked for one year if you reach 12 or more points in 12 months, 18 or more in 24 months, or 24 or more in 36 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A01
Reinstatement requirements after a point suspension or revocation differ depending on whether it was related to alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A01
To reinstate after a point suspension or revocation not related to alcohol, you submit SR-22 proof of insurance and pay a $20 reinstatement fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
After a point suspension or revocation related to intoxication, you meet the reinstatement requirements listed in the alcohol and drugs chapter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
Once your driving privilege is reinstated, the Department lowers your point total to four. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
After one year of driving with no new points, the remaining points are cut by one-third. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
After two years with no new points, the remaining points are cut by one-half. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
After three years with no new points, the points drop to zero. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A02
Even when your points reach zero, certain convictions stay on your driving record permanently. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A02
A conviction for driving during a suspension may lead to a one-year revocation of your driving privilege. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A02
Continuing to drive during a revocation can bring a felony conviction and another one-year revocation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A02
When you miss a court date for a traffic violation, the court notifies you and gives you 30 days to pay the fines before it tells the Driver License Bureau. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A02
If you still do not comply within those 30 days, the court notifies the Driver License Bureau and your driving privilege is suspended at once. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A02
A suspension for failing to appear lasts until the Bureau receives proof the ticket is paid and a $20 reinstatement fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A02
You can send the reinstatement requirements for a failure to appear suspension by mail to the Driver License Bureau or bring them to its central office in Jefferson City. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A02
A conviction for failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading students carries five points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A02
A first school bus offense brings a court-ordered suspension of 90 days, or another period the court sets. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A02
A second school bus offense within 5 years brings a 90-day suspension, and a third or later offense within 5 years brings 180 days. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

Misconceptions: the first point threshold brings only an advisory letter, not a suspension; points reaching zero does not erase every conviction from the record; paying the ticket alone does not lift a failure to appear suspension without the reinstatement fee; driving while revoked is treated more harshly than driving while suspended.
Mnemonics: advisory, suspension, revocation as the three rungs of the point ladder; one-third, one-half, zero as the three yearly steps of point reduction.
Glossary: point accumulation advisory means the warning letter sent when points start to build up; suspension means a temporary loss of the driving privilege; revocation means cancellation of the driving privilege for a set period; FACT means Failure to Appear in Court for Traffic Violations; DLB means the Driver License Bureau.
Dynamic facts: point values, thresholds, suspension lengths and reinstatement fees are statutory and can change, and the bureau's mailing address and office hours are agency contact details to refresh from the Department of Revenue.
